```{python}
#| tags: [parameters]

section = "A"  # one of the sections in data/gradebook.csv
```

```{python}
#| label: setup
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML

GRADEBOOK = Path("data/gradebook.csv")  # SYNTHETIC: invented for teaching
MIN_STUDENTS = 5  # never describe a smaller group: its figures would point at individuals
NAMES = {"quiz_1": "Quiz 1", "essay": "Essay", "quiz_2": "Quiz 2", "project": "Project"}


def claim(condition: bool, sentence: str) -> None:
    """Stop the render with `sentence` if the marks do not support it."""
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(f"The marks no longer support this sentence: {sentence}")


book = pd.read_csv(GRADEBOOK, dtype={"section": str})
sections = sorted(book["section"].unique())
if section not in sections:
    raise ValueError(f"section {section!r} is not in {GRADEBOOK}: one of {', '.join(sections)}")
assert list(book.columns) == ["student_id", "section", *NAMES], "unexpected gradebook columns"
assert not book.columns.str.contains("name").any(), "the gradebook must hold ids, not names"

marks = book.melt(id_vars=["student_id", "section"], var_name="assignment", value_name="mark")
mine = marks[marks["section"] == section]
size = mine["student_id"].nunique()
assert size >= MIN_STUDENTS, f"section {section} has {size} students, fewer than {MIN_STUDENTS}"


def describe(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mean, standard deviation and number submitted, per assignment, rounded as printed."""
    stats = frame.groupby("assignment", sort=False)["mark"].agg(["mean", "std", "count"])
    return stats.reindex(list(NAMES)).round({"mean": 1, "std": 1})


here, course = describe(mine), describe(marks)
# Every group the sheet describes, each assignment's submissions included, is large enough.
too_few = here.index[here["count"] < MIN_STUDENTS].tolist()
assert not too_few, (f"section {section}: fewer than {MIN_STUDENTS} submissions for "
                     f"{', '.join(too_few)}: the sheet would point at individuals")


def relation(a: float, b: float) -> str:
    """ "above", "below" or "level with", chosen from the rounded values the sheet prints, so
    the word cannot disagree with the numbers beside it (no guard needed: code chose it)."""
    return "above" if a > b else "below" if a < b else "level with"


position = {a: relation(here.loc[a, "mean"], course.loc[a, "mean"]) for a in NAMES}
spread = {a: {"above": "wider than", "below": "narrower than", "level with": "the same as"}[
    relation(here.loc[a, "std"], course.loc[a, "std"])] for a in NAMES}
above = sum(word == "above" for word in position.values())
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## SYNTHETIC: invented for teaching

Every mark on this sheet comes from `data/gradebook.csv`, a gradebook invented for teaching
by `scripts/make_gradebook.py`. No student, course or mark is real, and students are ids,
never names. The sheet shows only section totals, never one student.
:::

This sheet is for **Section `{python} section`**: `{python} size` students, against the
whole course of `{python} marks["student_id"].nunique()` students in
`{python} len(sections)` sections (`{python} ", ".join(sections)`). The section's
mean mark is above the course mean on `{python} above` of the
`{python} len(NAMES)` assignments (SYNTHETIC marks).

## Assignment by assignment

```{python}
#| output: asis
for a, name in NAMES.items():
    print(f"- **{name}**: a mean of {here.loc[a, 'mean']:.1f}, {position[a]} the course mean "
          f"of {course.loc[a, 'mean']:.1f}; a spread (standard deviation) of "
          f"{here.loc[a, 'std']:.1f}, {spread[a]} the course's {course.loc[a, 'std']:.1f}. "
          f"{here.loc[a, 'count']} of {size} submitted.")
```

Marks are out of 100. A mean leaves out work not submitted. The course includes this section.
With about twenty students a section, a difference of a few marks can be chance: this sheet
describes the marks and tests nothing.

::: {#tbl-marks}

```{python}
table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Assignment": list(NAMES.values()),
    f"Section {section}: mean (SD)": [f"{m:.1f} ({s:.1f})" for m, s in zip(here["mean"], here["std"])],
    "Course: mean (SD)": [f"{m:.1f} ({s:.1f})" for m, s in zip(course["mean"], course["std"])],
    "Difference": [f"{d:+.1f}" for d in (here["mean"] - course["mean"]).round(1) + 0.0],
    "Submitted": [f"{n} of {size}" for n in here["count"]],
})
HTML(table.to_html(index=False))
```

SYNTHETIC: invented for teaching. Section `{python} section` against the whole course: mean
mark out of 100 and standard deviation (SD), per assignment.

:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-means
#| fig-cap: "SYNTHETIC: invented for teaching. Mean mark per assignment, this section (blue circles) and the whole course (grey squares); each line spans one standard deviation either side of the mean."
#| fig-alt: "Dot chart with one row per assignment (Quiz 1, Essay, Quiz 2, Project) and marks out of 100 along the horizontal axis. Each row has a blue circle for this section's mean and a grey square for the course mean, each with a horizontal line spanning one standard deviation either side. The table above gives the same numbers."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 2.3), layout="constrained")
rows = range(len(NAMES))
for stats, offset, colour, marker, label in [
        (here, -0.12, "#0072B2", "o", f"Section {section}"),
        (course, 0.12, "#777777", "s", "Course")]:
    ax.errorbar(stats["mean"], [r + offset for r in rows], xerr=stats["std"], fmt=marker,
                color=colour, capsize=3, label=label)
ax.set_yticks(list(rows), list(NAMES.values()))
ax.invert_yaxis()
low = min((here["mean"] - here["std"]).min(), (course["mean"] - course["std"]).min())
ax.set_xlim(max(0, 10 * (low // 10) - 10), 100)  # marks are out of 100
ax.set_xlabel("Mark out of 100 (SYNTHETIC)")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
fig.legend(frameon=False, loc="outside upper center", ncols=2)
plt.show()
```
